cards.text: Jesus has just finished talking to the crowds about John the Baptist (Matthew 11:7-19). Now He turns to the cities where most of His miracles were performed, and He begins to denounce them. Friend, this is NOT a thank-you speech.

cards.question: Jesus denounces the cities that saw most of His miracles. What's the reason?

cards.text: Jesus starts with two towns: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida!" Two woes, back to back, like waking up to two missed calls from your boss before 8 a.m.

cards.question: Jesus says if the miracles done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, what would those cities have done?
Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Chorazin and Bethsaida than for Tyre and Sidon.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to Capernaum, the town He went to live in (Matthew 4:13). Talk about getting called out in your OWN neighborhood group chat.

cards.question: Jesus asks Capernaum if it will be lifted up to heaven. No, He says, it will be brought down to ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up Sodom, the city the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on (Genesis 19:24). Friend, when THAT'S the city you're being compared to, the meeting is not going well.

cards.question: If the miracles done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, what does Jesus say would have happened to Sodom?

answers.text: It would have remained to this day
It would have been destroyed sooner
It would have mocked Him just the same

cards.question: Jesus says the day of judgment will be more bearable for Sodom than for Capernaum.

cards.text: Then the whole tone changes. Jesus declares, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth," and He tells the Father why.

cards.question: Jesus praises the Father for hiding these things from the wise and learned. Who does the Father reveal them to?

cards.text: Jesus adds, "Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight."
Then He says all things have been entrusted to Him by His Father. And no one knows the Son except the Father.

cards.question: Jesus says no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

cards.text: And now, after all those woes, comes an invitation: "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened," Jesus says. Friend, that "all" covers everybody who has ever hit snooze FOUR times and then argued with the alarm.

cards.question: Jesus invites everyone who is weary and burdened to come to Him, and He promises to give them ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me," for He is gentle and humble in heart. Friend, that's the trainer EVERYBODY wants on day one of a new job, not the one who sighs every time you ask where the stapler is.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever takes His yoke and learns from Him will find ___ for their souls.
Jesus ends by telling why His yoke brings rest. How does He describe His yoke and His burden?
